It refuses a name where `FORBIDDEN_ALIAS_PATTERN` finds a quotation mark, whitespace, a control character, a semicolon, a hash or a comment marker; the quotation marks include square brackets (`django/db/models/sql/query.py:Query.check_alias`; [The SELECT clause: `get_select`, the select mask and `klass_info`](../sql/select.md#annotations-and-extras-the-masks)).

`Join.as_sql` writes that alias after the table (`django/db/models/sql/datastructures.py:Join.as_sql`; [`filter`, `exclude` and `Q` objects](../querysets/filters.md#filteredrelation-a-condition-in-the-join)).
`Query.add_filtered_relation` hands the name to the check, after refusing a name with a period (`django/db/models/sql/query.py:Query.add_filtered_relation`).
Its notes say `QuerySet.order_by` "was subject to SQL injection in column aliases containing periods" when a `FilteredRelation` used the same alias (`docs/releases/5.2.11.txt`).
At this commit it does so only for one that was (`django/db/models/sql/compiler.py:SQLCompiler._order_by_pairs`).

6.1 quotes the alias of every table and join with `SQLCompiler.quote_name`, and PostgreSQL's backend lost its own compiler for a SELECT (`django/db/backends/postgresql/compiler.py`; [What changed in expressions, lookups and the compiler](sql.md)).
The connector is the word `WhereNode.as_sql` writes between the conditions it joins (`django/db/models/sql/where.py:WhereNode.as_sql`).
`QuerySet._filter_or_exclude_inplace` refuses both keywords with `TypeError`, by `PROHIBITED_FILTER_KWARGS` (`django/db/models/query.py:QuerySet._filter_or_exclude_inplace`).

`Q._check_connector` also checks the connector given to `Q.create`, a class method by which Django builds `Q` objects of its own (`django/db/models/query_utils.py:Q.create`, `django/db/models/query_utils.py:Q._check_connector`).

Before 5.0.10 and 5.1.4 a `HasKey` made directly on Oracle "was subject to SQL injection if untrusted data was used as a lhs value" (CVE-2024-53908; `docs/releases/5.0.10.txt`).
